SOS Certificates On A Hypercube

Documents/Bernstein Mathematics/SOS Certificates

This page separates the polynomial representation from the certificate used to prove a matrix sign. For a residual F⪯0F\preceq0F⪯0, set S=−FS=-FS=−F; for F⪰0F\succeq0F⪰0, set S=FS=FS=F. The mathematical question is then

S(α)⪰0,α∈[0,1]ℓ.S(\boldsymbol\alpha)\succeq0, \qquad \boldsymbol\alpha\in[0,1]^\ell.S(α)⪰0,α∈[0,1]ℓ.

Scalar formulas extend to polynomial matrices through matrix-SOS Gram representations, or by applying the structured certificate to yTS(α)yy^{\mathsf T}S(\boldsymbol\alpha)yyTS(α)y. Positive-semidefinite Gram matrices certify non-strict inequalities. A strict margin must already be present in the residual; the package does not insert one.

Explore The Stored Constraint Shape

Section titled “Explore The Stored Constraint Shape”

Choose a selector and a source-valid residual shape below. Ordinary residuals have one active coefficient row per cell; rhodiff residuals have exactly 2ℓ2^\ell2ℓ rate-vertex rows. Semidefinite mode creates one matrix certificate per cell and active row. Entrywise mode creates an independent scalar Gram certificate for every entry of the displayed square residual.

A Tiny Example: Positive Polynomial, Failed Direct Test

Section titled “A Tiny Example: Positive Polynomial, Failed Direct Test”

Consider

p(α)=(α−12)2+0.1=α2−α+0.35.p(\alpha)=(\alpha-\tfrac12)^2+0.1 =\alpha^2-\alpha+0.35.p(α)=(α−21​)2+0.1=α2−α+0.35.

It is strictly positive on [0,1], with minimum 0.1. Its degree-two Bernstein representation is

p(α)=0.35B02(α)−0.15B12(α)+0.35B22(α).p(\alpha)=0.35B_0^2(\alpha)-0.15B_1^2(\alpha)+0.35B_2^2(\alpha).p(α)=0.35B02​(α)−0.15B12​(α)+0.35B22​(α).

The negative middle coefficient means the direct Bernstein test cannot prove positivity. It does not mean the polynomial is negative. A stronger box certificate can use the identity

p(α)=(α−12)2+0.1p(\alpha)=(\alpha-\tfrac12)^2+0.1p(α)=(α−21​)2+0.1

as a sum of squares with a positive constant. This one example explains why the package separates the stored polynomial from the certificate selected for it.

Full-Space SOS

Section titled “Full-Space SOS”

The simplest Gram certificate ignores the box and proves global nonnegativity:

p(z)=vd(z)TQvd(z),Q⪰0,p(z)=v_d(z)^{\mathsf T}Qv_d(z), \qquad Q\succeq0,p(z)=vd​(z)TQvd​(z),Q⪰0,

where vdv_dvd​ contains monomials through a selected degree. Coefficient matching is linear in QQQ. This is an SOS certificate on all of Rℓ\mathbb R^\ellRℓ, so it may be much stronger than positivity only on a box. It is sufficient, but a multivariate nonnegative polynomial need not be SOS. The package has no full-space SOS constructor.

Direct Bernstein Coefficient Certificate

Section titled “Direct Bernstein Coefficient Certificate”

On a local box, write

S(c)(α)=∑iBim(α)C(c)[i].S^{(\mathbf c)}(\boldsymbol\alpha)= \sum_{\boldsymbol i} B_{\boldsymbol i}^{m}(\boldsymbol\alpha)C^{(\mathbf c)}[\boldsymbol i].S(c)(α)=i∑​Bim​(α)C(c)[i].

Because the tensor Bernstein basis is nonnegative and sums to one,

C(c)[i]⪰0for every i⟹S(c)(α)⪰0on the box.C^{(\mathbf c)}[\boldsymbol i]\succeq0\quad\text{for every }\boldsymbol i \quad\Longrightarrow\quad S^{(\mathbf c)}(\boldsymbol\alpha)\succeq0 \quad\text{on the box}.C(c)[i]⪰0for every i⟹S(c)(α)⪰0on the box.

This is the default pdlmi constructor certificate after residual and rate-vertex assembly. It introduces no Gram matrices. The converse is false: an indefinite coefficient defeats this certificate, not the continuous inequality.

Pólya-Type Coefficient Relaxation

Section titled “Pólya-Type Coefficient Relaxation”

Pólya’s theorem concerns a homogeneous polynomial strictly positive on a simplex. After multiplication by a sufficiently high power of the sum of the simplex coordinates, all coefficients become positive. For each box axis, (1−αs,αs)(1-\alpha_s,\alpha_s)(1−αs​,αs​) is a point on a one-simplex and its entries sum to one. Therefore

∏s=1ℓ((1−αs)+αs)r=1\prod_{s=1}^{\ell} \bigl((1-\alpha_s)+\alpha_s\bigr)^r=1s=1∏ℓ​((1−αs​)+αs​)r=1

changes only the tensor Bernstein degree, not the residual. A higher degree can expose coefficient positivity that was not visible at the original degree.

applyPolya(r) implements one selected elevation increment followed by the same direct coefficient test. It does not search for an exponent, add a margin, or create SOS multipliers. Failure at one increment is inconclusive. Quantitative Pólya bounds also retain strict-positivity assumptions; see Powers and Reznick (2001).

Putinar Quadratic Modules

Section titled “Putinar Quadratic Modules”

For

K={z:gj(z)≥0, j=1,…,q},K=\{z:g_j(z)\ge0,\ j=1,\ldots,q\},K={z:gj​(z)≥0, j=1,…,q},

the quadratic module generated by the constraints contains polynomials

σ0(z)+∑j=1qσj(z)gj(z),σj SOS.\sigma_0(z)+\sum_{j=1}^{q}\sigma_j(z)g_j(z), \qquad \sigma_j\ \text{SOS}.σ0​(z)+j=1∑q​σj​(z)gj​(z),σj​ SOS.

Putinar’s Positivstellensatz states that every polynomial strictly positive on KKK has such a representation when the quadratic module is Archimedean. Compactness alone is not Putinar’s hypothesis. Truncating multiplier degrees produces finite SDP relaxations, but failure at one order is not a nonnegativity counterexample. See Putinar (1993).

Implemented Putinar selector

Section titled “Implemented Putinar selector”

In one parameter, the package dispatches applyPutinar to the exact parity-specific Markov–Lukács form described below. Its minimum and default order are ⌊m/2⌋\lfloor m/2\rfloor⌊m/2⌋, the same as applyFullBoxPreorder.

For two or more parameters, the package uses one fixed-order specialization on every local hypercube. With the axis generators hs=αs(1−αs)h_s=\alpha_s(1-\alpha_s)hs​=αs​(1−αs​), the sign-normalized target is represented as

S(α)=S0(α)+∑s=1ℓαs(1−αs)Ss(α).S(\boldsymbol\alpha)=S_0(\boldsymbol\alpha) +\sum_{s=1}^{\ell} \alpha_s(1-\alpha_s)S_s(\boldsymbol\alpha).S(α)=S0​(α)+s=1∑ℓ​αs​(1−αs​)Ss​(α).

For a target of stored degree mmm in two or more parameters, the absolute order satisfies

r≥⌈m2⌉.r\ge\left\lceil\frac m2\right\rceil.r≥⌈2m​⌉.

The no-argument method uses equality in either dimension case. For two or more parameters at order rrr, the unweighted Gram term uses tensor Bernstein basis degree r1r\mathbf1r1. The sssth multiplier uses r1−esr\mathbf1-\mathbf e_sr1−es​; blocks with a negative degree component are omitted. After multiplication by hsh_shs​, every term has tensor degree 2r12r\mathbf12r1. The stored target is elevated to that degree and matched exactly, coefficient by coefficient.

applyPutinar creates independent dense PSD Gram blocks and equalities for every physical cell and active rate row. It adds no strictness margin and does not call a solver. This callable path is not a general-domain or general-generator Putinar interface.

Schmüdgen And Full Preorderings

Section titled “Schmüdgen And Full Preorderings”

The preordering generated by g1,…,gqg_1,\ldots,g_qg1​,…,gq​ also includes every square-free product:

p(z)=∑ν∈{0,1}qσν(z)∏j=1qgj(z)νj,σν SOS.p(z)= \sum_{\nu\in\{0,1\}^{q}} \sigma_\nu(z) \prod_{j=1}^{q}g_j(z)^{\nu_j}, \qquad \sigma_\nu\ \text{SOS}.p(z)=ν∈{0,1}q∑​σν​(z)j=1∏q​gj​(z)νj​,σν​ SOS.

Schmüdgen’s Positivstellensatz gives such a representation for polynomials strictly positive on a compact basic closed semialgebraic set. Compared with a quadratic module, the full preordering can require many more multiplier blocks. See Schmüdgen (1991).

For the hypercube, the package uses the ℓ\ellℓ generators hs=αs(1−αs)h_s=\alpha_s(1-\alpha_s)hs​=αs​(1−αs​). Their nonnegative set is exactly [0,1]ℓ[0,1]^\ell[0,1]ℓ, and the 2ℓ2^\ell2ℓ subset products form the implemented box-specific full preordering. At a selected absolute order, applyFullBoxPreorder creates independent Gram blocks for every physical cell and active rate row, then matches the resulting Bernstein coefficients exactly. This is not a general-domain Schmüdgen interface.

F(a,b)=∑i=03∑k=03Bi3(a)Bk3(b)Fi,k.F(a,b)=\sum_{i=0}^{3}\sum_{k=0}^{3} B_i^3(a)B_k^3(b)F_{i,k}.F(a,b)=i=0∑3​k=0∑3​Bi3​(a)Bk3​(b)Fi,k​.

9n×9n,6n×6n,6n×6n,4n×4n,9n\mathbin{\times}9n,\quad 6n\mathbin{\times}6n,\quad 6n\mathbin{\times}6n,\quad 4n\mathbin{\times}4n,9n×9n,6n×6n,6n×6n,4n×4n,

One-Dimensional Markov–Lukács Forms

Section titled “One-Dimensional Markov–Lukács Forms”

On [0,1][0,1][0,1], interval nonnegativity has exact parity-specific forms. For degree at most 2d2d2d,

p(α)=vd(α)TQ0vd(α)+α(1−α)vd−1(α)TQ1vd−1(α),Q0,Q1⪰0.p(\alpha)= v_d(\alpha)^{\mathsf T}Q_0v_d(\alpha) +\alpha(1-\alpha) v_{d-1}(\alpha)^{\mathsf T}Q_1v_{d-1}(\alpha), \qquad Q_0,Q_1\succeq0.p(α)=vd​(α)TQ0​vd​(α)+α(1−α)vd−1​(α)TQ1​vd−1​(α),Q0​,Q1​⪰0.

For degree at most 2d+12d+12d+1,

p(α)=(1−α)vd(α)TQ0vd(α)+αvd(α)TQ1vd(α),Q0,Q1⪰0.p(\alpha)= (1-\alpha)v_d(\alpha)^{\mathsf T}Q_0v_d(\alpha) +\alpha v_d(\alpha)^{\mathsf T}Q_1v_d(\alpha), \qquad Q_0,Q_1\succeq0.p(α)=(1−α)vd​(α)TQ0​vd​(α)+αvd​(α)TQ1​vd​(α),Q0​,Q1​⪰0.

These forms characterize interval nonnegativity at the stated parity rather than supplying only one hierarchy level. The one-parameter full-box path uses their Bernstein-basis matrix-Gram counterpart.

Four Operations That Are Not Interchangeable

Section titled “Four Operations That Are Not Interchangeable”
  1. Higher decision degree enlarges the decision-function search space.
  2. Degree elevation re-expresses one fixed residual exactly.
  3. Physical subdivision re-expresses the residual on smaller cells.
  4. Higher Gram order enlarges a positivity certificate.

Only the second operation is performed by applyPolya; the fourth is selected at one explicit or default order by applyPutinar or applyFullBoxPreorder. Their method pages place unsupported adaptive and general-purpose boundaries beside the callable syntax.

Exact Software Boundary

Section titled “Exact Software Boundary”

The callable package boundary is limited to:

  • direct coefficient assembly;
  • fixed-increment Pólya elevation followed by direct assembly;
  • fixed-order Putinar assembly, using the parity-specific one-dimensional Markov–Lukács form or the separate box generators αs(1−αs)\alpha_s(1-\alpha_s)αs​(1−αs​) in two or more parameters; and
  • fixed-order full box preordering, sharing that one-dimensional form and using every generator-subset product in multiple parameters.

Full-space SOS, general-domain or general-generator Putinar modules, general-domain preorderings, adaptive order search or automatic escalation, adaptive subdivision, automatic strictness margins, and post-solve residual certificates are mathematical background, not public package APIs. Both no-argument Gram selectors use ⌊m/2⌋\lfloor m/2\rfloor⌊m/2⌋ in one parameter and ⌈m/2⌉\lceil m/2\rceil⌈m/2⌉ in two or more parameters. Their one-dimensional Markov–Lukács assembly is the same; their multiple-parameter generator sets differ as described above.
